card.hook: Picture Interlaken and Unterseen laid out below you like a tiny model town, with the Bernese Alps lined up at the far end of the valley. That's the view from Harder Kulm, and it's a show-off.
card.stand_here: Stand right at the phone icon on the map, on the observation platform beside the restaurant. Face south, looking over Interlaken and up the Lütschine valley.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the whole town and valley. Switch to 0.5x to get the platform railing in the foreground. Then try 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the Alps at the end of the valley.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines, put the horizon on the upper third line and keep the phone level so the valley doesn't look tilted.
card.best_time: Pick a clear day, because cloud can hide the peaks. Early morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light, but check the funicular running times first.
card.selfie_here: Head to the pointed far end of the Two Lakes Bridge (Zwei-Seen-Steg), beyond the restaurant terrace. It's the summit's signature platform and one guide singles out the tip as a good photo point. For something more fun, pose with the Swiss cow statue on the platform by the restaurant. Use the front camera, try 0.5x and let the view sit behind you.
card.ask_someone: Ask someone to stand at the far end of the Two Lakes Bridge and turn back toward the restaurant, so the whole building and both lakes fit in the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: Check the official site before you go for funicular running times and any ticket rules.
card.challenge: Get all three layers in one frame: town roofs in front, the valley floor in the middle and the high peaks behind. Bonus points if the horizon stays level.
card.good_to_know: Harder Kulm is 1,322 metres up, on the western end of the forested Harder ridge. The Harderbahn funicular climbs from Interlaken in about eight minutes. From the upper station it's about a five-minute walk to the restaurant and platform, so leave a little time for that last stretch.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand right at the phone icon on the map, on the observation platform beside the restaurant. Face south, looking over Interlaken and up the Lütschine valley.

selfie_spots.detail: on the cantilevered bridge at Harder Kulm, at its pointed tip beyond the restaurant terrace
selfie_spots.why: One guide singles out the bridge's pointed end as a good photo point, and the bridge is the summit's signature platform.

The ask-someone position comes from photographers' compositions for the bridge, not from a page stating where a passer-by should stand to photograph a visitor. card.hook: Every passenger service ends here, so Interlaken Ost is where the whole parade of trains, backpacks and big grins spills out. It's the perfect 'we've arrived' picture.
card.stand_here: Stand at the phone icon on the map, at the front of Interlaken Ost railway station, and face the station building. Try to get the Aare canal in the frame next to it, but check the exact spot when you're there.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for a natural view of the station front. If you can't step back far enough to fit the building and canal in, switch to zoom 0.5x. Zoom 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) is good for details like a train nose or the station name.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line the station building up with a horizontal line so it doesn't lean.
card.best_time: Go in daylight, in the morning or late afternoon, when the light is softer on the station front. Early in the day it's often quieter too.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera, switch to zoom 0.5x, and hold your phone a little lower and further out so the station building fits behind your shoulder. Take a few shots so you get one without a stranger photobombing.
card.rules_and_safety: This is a working railway station, so check the official site for any rules about photographing on the platforms. If you go onto the platforms, stay behind the platform lines and keep out of passengers' way.
card.challenge: Take a few frames as people walk past the station front, then pick the one where they make the building look properly big.
card.good_to_know: This station used to be called Interlaken Zollhaus. It got its present name in 1890, when the Bernese Oberland railway arrived and made it much busier. Three lines meet here: the BLS Thunersee line, the Zentralbahn Brünig line and the Bernese Oberland railway towards Lauterbrunnen and Grindelwald. Trains use two gauges (standard and metre), and ships on Lake Brienz have a quay at the station too.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the phone icon on the map, at the front of Interlaken Ost railway station, and face the station building. Try to get the Aare canal in the frame next to it, but check the exact spot when you're there.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a spot where the visitor has Interlaken Ost station behind them, so I am returning no selfie spots rather than guessing. Pages checked and why they don't qualify: Harder Kulm (reached by funicular, about a five-minute walk from the station; https://www.chasinghippoz.com/travel-photo-blog/interlaken-switzerland) is a mountain viewpoint with the station not in the frame. Höhematte in Interlaken is named as a selfie spot with the Jungfrau behind, but the station is not mentioned as part of that view (https://www.thunersee.ch/en/experiences/poi/fotopoints). The Swiss Selfie Museum at Bahnhofstrasse 24, Unterseen, is an indoor museum about 15 to 20 minutes' walk from the station, not a station view (https://evendo.com/locations/switzerland/interlaken/attraction/swiss-selfie-museum). The Aare-side pages (Schaalbrücke and the Aare Dam viewpoint, https://www.jenintheair.com/interlaken/) describe river views and do not mention the station. The Flickr and Wikimedia photos of the station show the building from various angles but are not guides to where to stand, so I did not use them. No page gave a passer-by position for photographing a visitor with the whole station in view, so ask_someone_spot is null. No page stated selfie stick or tripod rules, and no page gave a safety point for this station. The supplied coordinates (46.69045, 7.86900) match the station's Wikidata position (46°41'24"N, 7°52'8"E), so the station identification is consistent. A local search for the station's riverside frontage or the Aare bridge near the station might turn up a spot, but I could not verify one from the sources I reached.

card.hook: Here's the funny thing about the Harderbahn: the famous view from the top doesn't include the Harderbahn at all. You get the town, two lakes and three big peaks, and the little train stays out of the picture.
card.stand_here: Ride up and stand on the Zwei-Seen-Steg, at the summit by the upper station end, facing out over Interlaken with the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau behind it. Want the funicular itself in a photo? Save that for the lower station.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the town-and-lakes view, then try 0.5x to squeeze in more of the lakes. Zoom 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) pulls the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau closer.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on gridlines and keep the horizon level, with the town and lakes in the bottom half and the peaks above, then tap the mountains and drag the brightness down a touch so the sky keeps its colour.
card.best_time: Late afternoon or sunset, according to several guides. Check the last descent time at the station so you're not stuck up there after the view is over.
card.selfie_here: Try the bridge over the turquoise water just before the Harderbahn lower station, which one reviewer calls a lovely photo spot. Use the front camera, and glance at your screen to check the funicular really is behind you, because that isn't confirmed. At the top, the Zwei-Seen-Steg is another well-documented photo spot, so try zoom 0.5x there with the view over your shoulder.
card.rules_and_safety: The walkway is the popular spot, so expect company, and you can step to its sides for a quieter angle. The funicular is ticketed, and one blog says it closes from late November through March, so check the official site for the season and timetable before you go.
card.challenge: Get the full set: the lakes-and-peaks view from the top, plus the cars leaving the lower station with the station building in the frame.
card.good_to_know: The Harderbahn opened on 15 May 1908 and is 1,435 metres long. The track was laid in a gentle curve so it wouldn't scar the hillside, and the ride takes about ten minutes. The lower station sits at 550 metres, and the top station is a short walk from the Harder Kulm viewpoint at 1,321 metres.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Ride up and stand on the Zwei-Seen-Steg, at the summit by the upper station end, facing out over Interlaken with the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau behind it. Want the funicular itself in a photo? Save that for the lower station.

selfie_spots.name: Bridge just before the Harderbahn funicular, Interlaken
selfie_spots.detail: On the approach to the Harderbahn lower station, at the bridge over turquoise water
selfie_spots.why: A TripAdvisor reviewer calls this bridge a lovely photo spot, but the page does not confirm that the funicular is in the frame behind a visitor.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a spot where the Harderbahn itself is behind a selfie, and none names a spot where a passer-by should stand to frame a visitor with the whole funicular. The only named spot near the funicular is the bridge above, which comes from one reviewer's comment, so check on arrival that the funicular is actually in the background. The Interlaken tourism photo-point page recommends a selfie at the Höhematte with the snow-capped Jungfrau behind, but the funicular is not part of that framing, so I left it out. The Two Lakes Bridge at the Harder Kulm summit is a well-documented photo spot, but it is at the top, not at the funicular. One blog says the Harder Kulm funicular closes from late November through March, which matters for a visit in late November 2026; verify current hours.

card.hook: Cross the Aare from Interlaken and the crowds thin out fast. Suddenly you're in a lane of old wooden houses that looks like a film set.
card.stand_here: Stand at either end of Untere Gasse, the old main lane of Unterseen, and face down the street so the row of wooden houses fills your screen. Keep your phone level.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x so the street looks natural. Switch to 0.5x if the lane feels too narrow for all those facades, and try 2x for shutters, woodwork and window boxes.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line the house edges up with the vertical lines so the buildings don't lean.
card.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon is usually best, with softer light and fewer people. In the evening, the riverside views are worth a second look.
card.selfie_here: Try the Schaalbrücke over the Aare, which one guide names as a vantage point over Unterseen. Use the front camera at 0.5x and hold it a little low so the town fits over your shoulder. For an old-Swiss backdrop, the half-timbered houses in Obere Gasse also work nicely.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by on the Aare promenade on the Interlaken side to point their phone across the river at the old town and its church, with you in the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: Untere Gasse is a public street. If you also visit bridges or any buildings, check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Get the whole street in one shot with every house standing perfectly straight. No leaning towers allowed!
card.good_to_know: Unterseen was founded on 13 July 1279, after King Rudolf I von Habsburg gave permission for a stronghold between the two lakes. It burnt down in 1470, and Bern oversaw the rebuilding with the town house at the centre. Today about 5,760 people live here, and on a clear day you can see the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau from town.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at either end of Untere Gasse, the old main lane of Unterseen, and face down the street so the row of wooden houses fills your screen. Keep your phone level.

card.hook: Most towns keep their lawns small and polite. Interlaken has a huge green one right in the middle, with the snow-capped Jungfrau standing behind it like it's posing.
card.stand_here: Stand on the Höheweg promenade, at the Grand Tour of Switzerland photo spot near the Armin-Schärz-Brunnen. Face the Höhematte lawn so the grass fills the bottom of your screen and the Jungfrau rises behind it.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the lawn with the Jungfrau behind it. Go to 0.5x if you want the grand hotels along the promenade in the shot too. Try 2x-5x (depends on your phone) to bring the peaks closer or to pick out a paraglider coming in.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the mountains, then drag the brightness slider down a little so the snow keeps its detail instead of turning plain white.
card.best_time: Pick a clear day, because the Jungfrau is easy to lose in cloud. Early morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light on the peaks.
card.selfie_here: The official tourism pages send visitors to the Grand Tour of Switzerland photo spot on Höheweg, near the Armin-Schärz-Brunnen, for a selfie with the snow-capped Jungfrau behind them. Use the front camera and tilt it up a little so the mountain sits over your shoulder.
card.challenge: Take one shot from the promenade and one from out on the lawn, then pick a winner. Bonus points if a paraglider drops into the frame.
card.good_to_know: The Höhematte has been protected since 1864 and is a free public park. The Grand Tour of Switzerland marks the spot near the Armin-Schärz-Brunnen as the official photo spot. Paragliders sometimes land on the lawn, so if the foreground is busy or briefly blocked, wait a moment and try again.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the Höheweg promenade, at the Grand Tour of Switzerland photo spot near the Armin-Schärz-Brunnen. Face the Höhematte lawn so the grass fills the bottom of your screen and the Jungfrau rises behind it.

selfie_spots.name: Grand Tour of Switzerland photo spot on the Höhematte, Höheweg
selfie_spots.detail: On Höheweg near the Armin-Schärz fountain (Armin-Schärz-Brunnen), at the Höhematte park edge
selfie_spots.why: The official tourism pages send visitors to this Höhematte spot to take a selfie with the snow-capped Jungfrau behind them.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found says where a passer-by should stand to photograph a visitor with the whole Höhematte behind them, so ask_someone_spot is null. Addresses for the photo point conflict: the official German page places it on Höheweg near the Armin-Schärz fountain, while an Evendo listing gives Höheweg 57a, across from the Casino and near the park entrance. Paragliders land on the Höhematte, but no page I found gives a safety warning about it.

card.hook: A 2-minute ride in a creaky wooden car with curtains instead of glass, and you step out above two lakes. Not a bad trade for a short, steep hop up the hill.
card.stand_here: Stand near the restaurant terrace at the summit. The line of the railway lies about 157 m to the north-east of it, so face north-east and let the slope sit in the frame. Check on site that you're in the right spot.
card.zoom: Start at 0.5x to fit the plain, both lakes and the railway into one shot. Then try 1x for a calmer, more natural view, and 2x-5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the slope and the line of the rails.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines, put the horizon on the upper line and hold your phone level, because 0.5x bends a wonky horizon fast.
card.best_time: Pick a clear day so the lakes and mountains show up. Morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light than midday.
card.selfie_here: Flip to the front camera, try 0.5x and keep your arm slightly high, so the view spreads out behind your shoulder. Take a few frames and check that the horizon isn't tilted.
card.rules_and_safety: No photos or phone use during the toboggan ride, for safety reasons, so save your snaps for the terrace.
card.challenge: Take three pictures: the wide view from the terrace, the red-and-cream cars at the valley station, and a higher panorama from the observation tower. Then pick your favourite.
card.good_to_know: The Heimwehfluhbahn was built between 1904 and 1906. It's only 197 metres long, but it climbs 102 metres with a maximum gradient of 69%. The two wooden cars date from 1906, and the summit sits at 680 metres above sea level.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand near the restaurant terrace at the summit. The line of the railway lies about 157 m to the north-east of it, so face north-east and let the slope sit in the frame. Check on site that you're in the right spot.

selfie_research.safety: No taking photos or using phones during the toboggan ride, for safety reasons (Heimwehfluhbahn Summer Toboggan Run, https://ticketshopswitzerland.ch/tour/heimwehfluh/).
selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a place where a visitor can stand with the Heimwehfluhbahn funicular behind them, or where a passer-by can photograph a visitor with the whole funicular in frame. The pages describe the top terrace, the observation tower and the views, but none ties a photo spot to the cable car as the backdrop (e.g., https://airial.travel/attractions/switzerland/interlaken/heimwehfluh-interlaken-V7AmLHhH, https://www.guidle.com/de/ausfluege/interlaken/action/romantische-bahnfahrt_AZn4E8j). The Höhematte selfie in Interlaken (https://www.interlaken.swiss/en/experiences/poi/fotopoints) uses the Jungfrau as backdrop, not the funicular, so I left it out. The Harderbahn photo tip (https://holidaydestinations.net/travel-stories/scenic-views-best-spots-for-photography-in-interlaken.html) refers to a different funicular. No page I found mentions selfie-stick or tripod rules. Addresses conflict: the toboggan operator gives the valley meeting point as Därligenstrasse 32 (https://ticketshopswitzerland.ch/tour/heimwehfluh/), while other pages give Heimwehfluh 60 or Waldeggstrasse 89 (https://www.berneroberlandpass.ch/verkehrsmittel/heimwehfluh-interlaken, https://www.rexby.com/swissfamilyfun/ttd/HnOl2TrIRbm1Di7tnYDTwg). I could not check the coordinates you gave against any page. Because the valley station is only described as a few minutes' walk from Interlaken West station (https://www.interlaken.swiss/en/experiences/poi/heimwehfluh), a map check is needed before using any spot. Given these gaps, the on-site team should photograph the valley station directly or confirm a spot locally before publishing.

card.hook: Church, cloister and stately house, all sharing one patch of lawn. Interlaken Monastery looks like three buildings that couldn't agree on a style, and that's exactly why it makes a good photo.
card.stand_here: Stand in front of the castle church (Schlosskirche) at Schloss Interlaken and face south, where the monastery buildings are a very short way off, about 1 minute on foot. The church steeple and the 14th-century tower should rise above the lawns with the mountains behind.
card.zoom: Start at 1x to fit the whole group of buildings in. Tap 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) for just the steeple and tower, and use 0.5x only if you're standing close and can't fit everything in.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the steeple on one of the vertical lines and keep your phone level so the tower doesn't lean.
card.best_time: Morning or late afternoon light usually flatters the stonework, so aim for one of those if your day allows.
card.selfie_here: Try the old courtyard, standing by the arches of the Gothic cloister gallery. Use the front camera, hold it a little below eye level and let the arches fill the space over your shoulder. I couldn't confirm an exact selfie spot here, so treat it as a good place to experiment.
card.rules_and_safety: Parts of the complex are government offices and the interior is restricted, so keep to the exterior and the cloister.
card.challenge: Find the spot where the steeple sits on a gridline with the mountains right behind it, then see if you can catch two different building styles in the same shot.
card.good_to_know: Augustinian canons lived here from about 1133 until 1528, when the monastery was closed during the Reformation. In 1746-50 the west wing was pulled down and the newer castle built in its place, and the castle is still the administrative centre of the Interlaken district. The whole site is now a Swiss heritage site of national significance.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in front of the castle church (Schlosskirche) at Schloss Interlaken and face south, where the monastery buildings are a very short way off, about 1 minute on foot. The church steeple and the 14th-century tower should rise above the lawns with the mountains behind.

selfie_spots.name: Gothic cloister courtyard, Monastery and Interlaken Castle grounds
selfie_spots.detail: in the old courtyard, standing by the Gothic cloister gallery arches
selfie_spots.why: The only named monastery feature that pages describe as a photo area is the courtyard and cloister, but no page confirms a selfie position with the building behind the visitor.

sources.title: Monastery, castle church and Interlaken Castle

selfie_research.notes: Low confidence: no page I found names a selfie position with the monastery directly behind the visitor, and none names a spot where a passer-by should stand to frame the visitor with the whole monastery. The cloister courtyard is the closest match, and it is inferred from the pages' statements that the cloister and exterior are the best photo areas. The Yash Chopra statue is the most-photographed feature near the site, but sources conflict on its location. Airial says it is on the monastery grounds, while Tripadvisor, Holidify, Wanderlog and Evendo place it in the Kursaal Garden at Höheweg 71. The listed statue coordinates (46.687737, 7.858742) are roughly 400 m west of the position you gave, so I did not use it as a spot. Höhematte is recommended for selfies with the Jungfrau, but no page says the monastery is in that frame. Reviews mention that sprinklers in the Kursaal garden can wet visitors near the statue; I did not count this as a safety point. No page I found gives selfie stick or tripod rules.

card.hook: Most ruins make you pick between old stones and a big view. Unspunnen Castle gives you both: a round tower in front of you and the Jungfrau massif standing behind it.
card.stand_here: Stand at Unspunnen Castle, right where the phone icon sits on the map. Once you're inside the walls, you're in place. Face the open rampart side towards the Jungfrau, with the tower and old walls in front of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the tower and walls with the mountains behind. Go to 0.5x when you're close to the stonework and want the whole courtyard or rampart in the shot. Try zoom 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) to bring the Jungfrau closer.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the tower or a bit of wall on one third, and let the mountains and valley fill the other two thirds.
card.best_time: Pick a clear day so the Jungfrau massif shows up. If cloud hides the peaks, don't give up: the ruin still makes a good close-up of stone, walls and sky.
card.selfie_here: Head into the ruin's inner courtyard and stand with the round tower behind you. It's the most intact part of the castle, so it makes a strong backdrop. Use the front camera, and try 0.5x if your phone has it, to fit more tower in.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the meadow beside the castle, where the 1805 festival was held, while you pose near the ruin, so the whole tower and walls fit in the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: The ground is uneven, so wear sturdy shoes and watch your footing while you frame a shot. Some areas get slippery after rain, and the handrail around the tower leaves an unprotected drop on the outside.
card.challenge: Find an opening or an edge of wall and use it as a natural frame around the mountains.
card.good_to_know: The castle was probably built in the early 12th century, and the name Uspunnun first appears in records in 1232. It was left to fall into disrepair after 1762. The Unspunnenfest of 1805 made it famous and led to regular cleaning and repairs, and the festival of traditional Swiss competitions is still held in the fields below.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at Unspunnen Castle, right where the phone icon sits on the map. Once you're inside the walls, you're in place. Face the open rampart side towards the Jungfrau, with the tower and old walls in front of you.

selfie_spots.name: Inside the ruin, in front of the central round tower
selfie_spots.detail: in the ruin's inner courtyard, with the round tower behind you
selfie_spots.why: The walls of the central round tower, parts of the ring walls and the two residential wings can still be admired. That tower is the most intact feature, so it makes the strongest backdrop, though no page names this exact selfie position.

ask_someone_spot.name: The meadow next to the Unspunnen ruin
ask_someone_spot.detail: on the meadow beside the castle, where the 1805 festival was held, so the whole tower and walls fit in the frame

selfie_research.notes: Only one selfie spot could be supported. The pages describe the ruin and its views but do not name a specific selfie vantage, so the courtyard spot is inferred from the tower description and a courtyard photo filename. The meadow is named only as 'next to the imposing site', so confirm its exact boundaries on a map. The coordinates you gave match the ruin (Wikipedia lists 46.66861, 7.85722). No page states selfie stick or tripod rules.
